PullRequest.Title: scm: don't re-run git when switching back to an unchanged tab
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #350654

**Before:** Every time you switched back to a tab, VS Code ran 4 git processes to rebuild the file's change bars in the gutter, even when nothing had changed. For a file with changes, the bars were missing for a moment after each switch. VS Code dropped a file's change information as soon as its tab was hidden, and rebuilt it from git when the tab was shown again.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6cf4fc7-26dc-4c64-8da4-c7aa5939f774

**After:** The change information of a tab you leave is kept for a minute, paused. Switching back reuses it: no git process runs, and the change bars show up together with the file. If the file or the repository changed while the tab was hidden, the bars are recomputed once when you switch back.

Measured locally in Code OSS on a clone of the vscode repository, with 10 switches between two tabs:

- git processes: 40 → 0, counted with a debugger breakpoint where the git extension starts git.
- How long the change bars were missing after switching back to a file with changes: 0.3–0.8 s → 0 ms (median of 10 switches, two runs before the fix). Timed in the page from the click until the bars were drawn.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3fb7083d-33d1-49fd-b1a4-84375990f514

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Root cause**

- `QuickDiffWorkbenchController` holds a `QuickDiffModel` reference for each visible editor and for the active editor. Hiding a tab released the last reference, and `QuickDiffModelReferenceCollection` disposed the model, including its reference to the `git:` original text model.
- Showing the tab again created a new model. It called `provideOriginalResource`, which runs `git check-ignore`, and resolved the original again: `GitFileSystemProvider.stat` runs `git ls-files --stage` and `git cat-file -s`, and `readFile` runs `git show :<path>`.

**Fix** (`quickDiffModel.ts`)

- When the last reference is released, the model is suspended and kept instead of disposed. A kept model is disposed after 60 s, when more than 10 are kept (oldest first), or right away when its text file model is disposed (the file is closed).
- Acquiring a reference for the same text file model resumes the kept model and returns it.
- While suspended, `triggerDiff` only marks a diff as pending (a scheduled diff is cancelled and marked pending). `resume` runs one diff if one is pending. If the text changed meanwhile, it first clears the changes, so old decorations are never drawn on the wrong lines.
- `QuickDiffModelService` is now `Disposable`, so kept models are disposed with it.

**Trade-offs and alternatives**

- A kept model holds its original text model for up to 60 s. Changes in `.git` (stage, commit, checkout) still reload the originals of kept models, as they do for visible editors. That work is then already done when you switch back.
- The 60 s and 10 model limits are judgment calls for switching between a handful of tabs.
- Caching in the git extension (check-ignore results, object details, content) would need its own invalidation, and would still run the provider and the diff on every switch. Keeping the model avoids both, for every quick diff provider.

**Validation**

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/test/browser/quickDiffModel.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadQuickDiff.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadDocumentsAndEditors.test.ts`: 15 passing. The 2 new tests in `quickDiffModel.test.ts` fail without the fix.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/quickDiffModel.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/test/browser/quickDiffModel.test.ts`: passed.
- Manually in Code OSS, with dbgjs breakpoints counting git spawns in the extension host and quick diff model creation and reuse in the renderer:
  - 10 switches between `strings.ts` and `arrays.ts`, as in the issue: 40 → 0 git processes; 10 models created → 10 kept models reused.
  - Staging and then unstaging the file while its tab was hidden: on switching back, the bars changed to the staged style, and then back.
  - Closing a hidden tab disposes its kept model right away.
  - Show Next Change (the quick diff peek) works on a reused model.
  - A working tree change (an untracked file created and deleted, with Git: Refresh after each) starts the same git processes as before the fix.
  - A heap snapshot after ~150 switches has 2 quick diff models. An extension host CPU profile of 10 switches spends ~2 ms in the git extension (~81 ms before the fix).

</details>

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Static call-flow proof: ThrottledDelayer delegates isTriggered/cancel exclusively to Delayer; Throttler.queue stores a follow-up factory until its active promise settles; diff() tests disposal but not suspension. The old disposal cleared that factory. Only the frequency and duration of overlapping diffs are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: One queued provider-discovery pass and full worker diff computations for the hidden model, plus Git check-ignore for a normal tracked Git file.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: At most one already-queued follow-up per suspended model because Throttler coalesces queued factories; that follow-up computes each eligible provider original sequentially and its CPU cost grows with file/diff size. Independent suspended models can each retain such a follow-up; the cache caps retained models at ten. Warm original references avoid re-resolving git: files but do not cache getOriginalResource across completed diffs.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary background CPU and provider I/O, with extra latency for visible-editor operations sharing the editor worker.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Releasing the last reference disposed the model and its ThrottledDelayer, clearing the queued follow-up so it did not discover providers or compute a new hidden-file diff. A worker computation already dispatched before disposal was not cancelled; that unchanged limitation is not the reported regression.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After a pending debounce has elapsed and queued a follow-up behind an active diff, hiding the tab retains the model and lets that queued diff run even though the model is suspended. The suspension guard in triggerDiff() only rejects new submissions; the queued async factory and diff() do not check suspension.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The final-reference release now calls object.suspend() at quickDiffModel.ts:105 rather than disposing the object. Added suspend():267 checks only ThrottledDelayer.isTriggered() and :268 calls cancel(), both of which affect only the debounce timer (async.ts:517-523). It leaves an already-queued Throttler factory live. Before the diff, QuickDiffModel.dispose() called super.dispose(), which disposed the ThrottledDelayer's Throttler and cleared its queuedPromiseFactory (async.ts:293-295,526-528).
Findings.Title: Skip already-queued diffs when a model is suspended
Findings.Impact: Edit a file while a slow provider or substantial diff is still running, let the follow-up's 200 ms debounce expire, then switch tabs before the active diff completes. The hidden tab runs one unnecessary follow-up: normally another Git check-ignore and one worker diff per eligible original, despite nobody displaying it. This consumes CPU and worker capacity needed by the newly visible editor.
Findings.Evidence: async.ts:252-276 queues the latest factory when a diff is active and starts it on completion. ThrottledDelayer.trigger at :514 transfers the task into that queue after its 200 ms debounce; isTriggered at :517-519 only reflects the now-expired timer. quickDiffModel.ts:338-339 executes the queued factory without checking _suspended, and diff():360-395 re-queries providers and calls computeDiff for each eligible original. getQuickDiffsPromise():476-536 only shares in-flight discovery, not completed provider requests. EditorWorkerService.computeDiff at editorWorkerService.ts:110-112 dispatches to the shared editor worker. The new tests release before a diff starts or after it finishes, so they do not cover this overlap.
Findings.Recommendation: Check _suspended when the delayed/queued factory actually starts, mark _diffPending and skip diff() while suspended. Preserve the single resume-triggered recomputation; similarly re-check suspension before issuing worker work after awaited provider resolution.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Releasing the final reference on each tab switch immediately disposed a reusable quick-diff model and its git: original, forcing provider discovery, original-file resolution and worker diff computation every time the unchanged tab became visible again.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Repeated unchanged tab switches ran check-ignore, ls-files, cat-file and git show for each cold reconstruction and delayed gutter decoration availability behind provider/original resolution and diff computation; this call path is established statically.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Keep at most ten released models for sixty seconds, reuse them for the same text-file model and options, and request a diff on resume only after an invalidation or changed text version; unchanged warm tab switches avoid provider IPC, Git processes, original resolution and worker diff computation.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: QuickDiffWorkbenchController.onEditorsChanged (quickDiffDecorator.ts:423-466) releases decorators when an editor becomes hidden, and onDidActiveEditorChange:354-381 releases the active editor's reference. ReferenceCollection.acquire (lifecycle.ts:700-705) destroys the object at the last release. Base quickDiffModel.ts:69 unconditionally disposed it, releasing original model references via QuickDiffModel.dispose and its DisposableStore. Showing it again constructed a model and triggered getOriginalResource/getQuickDiffsPromise. For a tracked unstaged Git file, GitQuickDiffProvider.provideOriginalResource performs workspace.fs.stat and repository.checkIgnore; resolution of its git: original performs GitFileSystemProvider.stat/getObjectDetails (ls-files plus cat-file) and readFile/buffer (git show). Added quickDiffModel.ts:83-89 reuses the same suspended object, and triggerDiff:332-334 coalesces invalidations while hidden. The added reuse test verifies provider request counts [1,1,1,2] across release/reacquire and invalidation. Blame of the old unconditional disposal identifies the ReferenceCollection introduction and dirtyDiffModel.ts origin.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an editor or switch back to an unchanged hidden tab
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor display does not await quick diff, but gutter decorations and quick-diff navigation depend on provider discovery, original resolution and worker computation on a cold model. A warm retained model returns its existing changes synchronously without crossing these boundaries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke relevant quick-diff providers through extension-host RPC; Git providers inspect the working file and invoke repository.checkIgnore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: P provider calls per cold discovery pass; zero on an unchanged warm cache hit. Built-in working-tree Git discovery performs a filesystem stat and one check-ignore process for an eligible tracked file; staged discovery adds a filesystem stat but may return no original.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each return after final-reference release caused a new discovery pass; the PR avoids it on warm unchanged reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold gutter availability awaits provider completion; warm unchanged reuse removes this dependency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve original text models through filesystem-provider RPC and Git object reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolution per eligible provider result, sharing original text models by URI. A normal cold git: index original entails stat/getObjectDetails (ls-files and cat-file) plus readFile/buffer (git show). Warm retained originals require no new resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Last-reference disposal released original references, so subsequent unchanged switches normally repeated Git resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold gutter calculation waits for original content; warm unchanged reuse does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize models to the shared editor worker and compute document diffs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker diff per eligible provider original on cold calculation; zero for an unchanged retained-model hit. Synchronization sends initial text only for unsynchronized models and incremental changes thereafter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A new model scheduled computation on each unchanged tab return; warm reuse eliminates it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gutter results await computation but ordinary editor opening does not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct resource/options keys visited, relevant providers P after root/selector filtering, and distinct original URIs U after resolver sharing. Normal tracked unstaged Git files have one eligible original; staged files can have a second HEAD original. Up to ten unreferenced models are retained for sixty seconds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: References for the same canonical resource and serialized options share one model. Relevant providers are queried with Promise.allSettled; original references are resolved with Promise.all; worker diffs run sequentially within a model. Models are independent, with a shared editor worker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold, expired, evicted or replaced text-file models reconstruct. Warm unchanged reacquisition resumes the identical model and does no discovery or computation. Provider promises share only in-flight discovery; completed discovery is not permanently cached. Empty-provider results are reused by unchanged retained models, but invalidation permits discovery again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reference ownership, reconstruction, provider lookup, resolver behavior and shared-worker calls are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual cold provider and Git process durations depend on repository, platform and provider. No benchmark execution was performed.
Scenarios.Verdict: The normal warm tab-switch path fixes a concrete cache-lifecycle regression. The removed final-release mechanism was blamed and recorded through report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Modify a hidden file or change providers/configuration, then return to its tab
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Suspended triggerDiff records pending work. Reacquisition clears changes synchronously if the modified text version differs, then schedules one debounced recomputation. Fresh gutter information waits for provider discovery and worker calculation; the editor itself can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-query providers and inspect working-file eligibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider pass on resume after one or many hidden invalidations; built-in eligible working-tree Git performs one check-ignore plus filesystem stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hidden models were absent; returning constructed a model and queried providers regardless of invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fresh gutter information awaits it; no discovery is issued merely by new triggerDiff calls while suspended.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve changed or newly discovered provider originals, crossing filesystem RPC and Git subprocess boundaries for built-in Git.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero new original resolutions when provider IDs/URIs match; otherwise resolution for returned originals, sharing by URI through the resolver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold reconstruction normally resolved originals again even if their URI had not changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Recomputation waits only if new original content must be resolved.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One computation per eligible provider original in the coalesced resume pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Returning always required a newly scheduled diff. The PR retains that work only when pending or text versions differ.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fresh gutter results await the worker; ordinary editor display is not blocked.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Any number of hidden invalidations yields one resume-triggered calculation for each reacquired cached resource/options key. Calculation scales with relevant providers and file/diff size, not the number of hidden events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hidden invalidations coalesce into one boolean. Resume uses the existing 200 ms ThrottledDelayer and per-model Throttler. Provider discovery is concurrent across relevant providers; worker computations are sequential per model.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing original models are reused if discovered provider IDs and original URIs are unchanged. Provider discovery is repeated after pending invalidation, including empty previous results. Text-file identity mismatch discards the cached quick-diff model.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: suspended guard and resume pending/version paths are direct additions, and original equality reuse is directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Number of contributed providers and diff sizes varies; invalidation coalescing is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression in ordinary pending-event coalescing. Queued work that has already crossed the debounce boundary is analyzed separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit while a slow diff is running, let a follow-up queue, then hide the tab
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the running diff settles, its Throttler starts the already-queued follow-up even though the tab is now suspended. The hidden result is off its own UI critical path, but the shared worker performs CPU work that competes with visible-editor worker requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-query providers for the hidden model and execute Git eligibility checking.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unnecessary provider pass per retained queued follow-up, not an unbounded event queue. Normal tracked Git incurs another check-ignore and provider filesystem stat; warm original models do not incur the full cold Git reconstruction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Final-reference disposal disposed ThrottledDelayer and its Throttler, clearing the queued factory before it could issue this provider pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unneeded hidden work consumes extension-host/process resources while the user works in another tab.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch and compute full diffs for the now-hidden tab.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker computation per eligible original in that single follow-up. There is no document-diff result cache on this dispatch path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The already-queued follow-up was cleared on disposal. Worker computation already dispatched before disposal was not cancelled, and that pre-existing limitation is not reported.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extra diff CPU consumes the shared editor worker, increasing latency for visible-editor work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One queued follow-up per affected suspended model, with up to ten retained models. Each pass queries P relevant providers and computes each eligible original sequentially. CPU scales with file/diff complexity. An active diff lasting long enough for another debounce to expire is the trigger.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The 200 ms Delayer hands follow-ups to Throttler.queue. At most one follow-up factory is retained per active model. suspend checks/cancels only the Delayer timer, not an already-enqueued factory. Different cached models remain independent; worker execution shares one editor worker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The queued pass starts after the active pass, so completed provider discovery is reissued. Unchanged original URIs normally reuse warm original models and avoid Git original stat/readFile; this does not avoid working-tree provider check-ignore or worker calculation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: Delayer.isTriggered/cancel, Throttler.queue/dispose and the unguarded queued diff factory prove the before/after mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Overlap frequency and milliseconds of extra CPU are unmeasured. Larger diffs and slower provider responses make the trigger more likely; normal decoration computations have a 1000 ms per-diff budget.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity missing-coalescing performance regression, anchored to the new suspension timer-only check.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stage, commit, checkout or otherwise invalidate Git originals while recently visited tabs are hidden
Scenarios.CriticalPath: GitFileSystemProvider coalesces repository changes for 1100 ms and reloads live git: text models through TextFileEditorModelManager. This warming is background work, not awaited by the Git command or ordinary editor display. Returning to an invalidated cached tab still needs its coalesced diff computation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Keep hidden originals subscribed to repository-wide invalidation and reload their Git content through filesystem-provider RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For each affected live index original, object stat uses ls-files plus cat-file and content read uses git show; HEAD originals use ls-tree plus git show. Calls are per distinct live URI after repository-event grouping and per-URI queue coalescing, not per raw watcher event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Original models owned only by hidden quick-diff models were disposed and did not reload, although Git's URI notification cache could still emit their change events. Originals held by other consumers already reloaded before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background process/I/O and decoding work can contend with foreground work, but the repository command does not await these reloads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: U distinct retained original URIs affected by changed repository roots, excluding those already retained by another visible consumer. U depends on at most ten cached resource/options models and eligible providers; normal unstaged Git has one index original per file and staged files may also have a HEAD original. Multiple repository events within the debounce interval form one batch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository roots and URI events are grouped before emission. Text-file reloads serialize per original URI and retain at most one running plus one queued reload. Distinct URI keys are independent; Repository.run tracks read-only operations without a global limiter, and Git.exec/stream spawn directly.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitFileSystemProvider.cache stores URI/timestamp notification rows, not object bytes or details. Its new mtime defeats old text-model etags on an invalidation batch. Retained quick-diff originals stay live and are automatically reloaded; the quick-diff suspension guard suppresses subsequent computations, not filesystem reloads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the increased retained-original reload cardinality and background placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cost varies with distinct retained originals, repository event batches and Git/textconv duration. This is bounded by cache lifetime/count but not a byte budget.
Scenarios.Verdict: Recognized as the change's intentional bounded original-cache warming tradeoff, not a separate accidental bug. No new awaited command path or unbounded fan-out was found. The independently unintended queued diff computation is reported separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close files, expire/evict cached models, dispose the service, or use quick-diff navigation/peek
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Closing an unreferenced text-file model, timeout or oldest-entry eviction disposes its cache entry and original references. Navigation/peek acquires the same keyed model; warm unchanged data is available immediately, while cold or invalidated data follows the discovery/computation path above.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Release original model references or reacquire a quick-diff model for navigation/peek.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No new provider/Git/worker calls on unchanged warm navigation. Original reference disposal triggers asynchronous resolver lifecycle cleanup per distinct original URI; later cold reacquisition incurs the same discovery/resolution boundaries described above.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Last release immediately performed model cleanup and subsequent navigation reconstructed it. The PR delays this bounded cleanup and reuses warm models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup generally does not wait on subprocess/network work. Warm navigation avoids discovery latency; expired/cold navigation does not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most ten idle cache entries, sixty seconds per idle interval, distinct original text models and retained diff changes per entry. Active models remain owned by their normal references.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cache cleanup is synchronous and handles at most ten retained entries on service disposal. Resolver cleanup awaits original model promises/canDispose independently. Navigation and decorations share references for identical resource/options keys; there is no extra cache entry per editor instance.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reuse cancels the prior expiry timer and close listener; release restarts its idle interval and reinserts it as newest. Text-file identity mismatch, closure, expiry and capacity eviction dispose retained models. Service disposal clears all currently unreferenced models.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cache insertion/removal, timer cancellation, close listener and explicit original-reference disposal ownership are traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Memory per retained entry depends on text size, provider count and diff changes. Retention is count/time-bounded rather than byte-bounded; no independently established leak or catastrophic realistic input was identified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence cleanup or retention bug found. The bounded memory/lifetime increase is intrinsic to the intended cache.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Submitted one high-confidence medium finding: suspension fails to suppress a follow-up already queued behind an active diff. Recorded the unchanged-tab cache fix and its blamed introducing commit. Traced tab/peek reference ownership, pending-event coalescing, Git filesystem reloads, per-URI queues, shared worker dispatch and cache cleanup. Built-in Git paths contain no added database/network boundary; arbitrary extension-provider internals cannot be exhaustively characterized from this diff. Static review only; timings and resource magnitudes remain unmeasured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
